steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C).
Combine 1 1/2 cups white sugar, butter or margarine, vanilla and eggs. Mix well.

Stir in flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt. Blend well. Shape dough into 1 inch balls. Combine 2 tablespoons sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon. Roll dough in sugar/cinnamon mixture and place 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets. Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until set. Immediately remove from cookie sheets.

raw_recipe.headline: Snickerdoodles III

review.reviewBody: Snickerdoodles are my favorite cookie so I have tried 20+ recipes. This one is great HOWEVER turn the oven down a little - a tad below 375 degrees and be sure to use small scoops. Too big and they won't cook in the center. Always use room temp butter and eggs use the freshest ingredients possible and of the best quality you can afford.

These turned out delicious! I added a pinch of cinnamon to the dough. I rolled the dough balls in the cinnamon sugar and used a fork to make a crisscross shape to flatten the cookies. 375 degrees for 10 minutes and they were perfect. I didn't think rolling the balls in the cinnamon sugar added enough flavor, so after rolling and flattening I sprinkled a little more on top.

I made these for the first time last night. I used 1/2 butter and no shortening and used baking powder/soda mix instead of cream of tarter. I increased the vanilla to 2 Tbsp. and the flour to an even 3 cups. The roll mixture I used was 3 Tbsp. sugar, 2 tsp. cinnamon, 1/4 tsp. ginger and 1/4 tsp. nutmeg. Drop the temp to 375 for 9 minutes. I love the puffiness and texture! Very eye pleasing and tasted great!

Turned out absocinnamonlutely delicious! I added a few dashes of cinnamon to the sugar and egg mixture. I also wrapped the dough in wax paper and put it in the refrigerator for a half hour before baking. And I don't believe in ungreased cookie sheets or removing cookies immediately.

I used self rising flour so I left out the baking soda and salt. These are my favorite cookies! Easy or I would not make them. I used a small cookie scoop so they would all be the same size, making 35 generous sized cookies. I hate making cookies but will make these because they are so worth it. Addictive.

Turn oven down to 375, shorten cooking time, and press balls.
This was a great recipe. I doubled it and made 1/2 inch for a bake sale made about 125 cookies. They do not spread at all so be sure to push them down, but you can pack your tray. I baked them at 375 in convection for about 6 minutes turning once for even exposure to the fan.

My boyfriend's fav cookies are snickerdoodles. I tried about 4 or 5 recipes and this is by far the best tasting and easiest. His 96 yo mother can't chew anything hard so I use the convection oven, bake for 6 minutes and they come out and stay soft. I've added this recipe to my recipe box (yes, I use an actual recipe box with cards and everything LOL) but I ALWAYS include the URL and who made the recipe bcz i have to give credit where credit is due. Thank you Sue W!

This is my favorite snickerdoodle recipe. I recently had to alter the recipe to accommodate a friend who has a dairy allergy. I substituted butter with 1/3C butter flavored Crisco, substituted eggs with 6T of natural applesauce and upped flour to 3C. They still came out fabulous. On another side note: I do flatten them a little before I put them in the oven.

I read a lot of comments both before and after I made these (yesterday) and I have come to the conclusion that not many other people figured out that there’s just too much frickin’ flour—2-3/4 cups is overkill. And that’s why the dryness and “failure to spread” of the individual cookies in the oven. I added 2 cups of flour and think it would be even better with a little less than that. The flavor of these cookies is superb, and my batch with 3/4 cup less flour was very good, but I’m going to make them with 9-year-old and 7-year-old boys on Thursday so I’ll see if (1) they’re better with less flour than 2 cups, and (2) are they good to make with kids. If it seems worthwhile, I’ll post the answers.

Great recipe with some modifications. After reading the reviews, I swapped the cream of tartar and the baking soda with 1.5 teaspoons of baking powder (I dont like the sour taste of cream of tartar). I smushed dough balls slightly with a fork and baked for 10 minutes at 375. They turned out perfect...slight crunch but soft in the middle.
Easy recipe and a perfect cookie. I did add 1/2 teaspoon vanilla with the eggs.

I kept the same amount of flour but added one egg, I also used self rising flour instead of all purpose flour. Try adding a little allspice to the cinnamon & sugar coating. I baked them at 350 for about 14 minutes. They are so soft and stayed that way!! This recipe is fantastic!!!

These are fantastic! I was specifically looking for a recipe that does not call for shortening and this did not disappoint. The only change I made was reducing the temp to 375 and adding 2 minutes. This left the cookies pillowy soft in the middle with a hint of crisp around the edges.

My mom, grandma, great grandma, great great grandma and so on have been making the same snickerdoodle recipe for decades, but I didn't have shortening so I tried this one. Don't tell Grandma, but this one is better! The only thing I changed was temperature. I did 9ish minutes at 375.
So easy and cookies are delicious
I think the addition of butter tastes better.
If you’re thinking about using this recipe, do not. Bottom tier snickerdoodles
These flattened out like pancakes. Not a great recipe.
easy recipe, my picky snickerdoole husband loves them.
Soft! Super easy ingredients and amazing.
